speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when these gait and limb coordination problems first started, and have they been getting worse gradually or all at once? Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or muscle weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol use or vitamin deficiencies, and are you experiencing any headaches, nausea, or recent head injuries? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your balance when standing still or any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning a shirt?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your Crohn's history and recent natalizumab use, do you have any new neurological symptoms like vision changes, numbness, or weakness that might suggest an infection or demyelinating process? I would like to request an MRI of your brain and spine to evaluate for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy or other central nervous system issues. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_and_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. Neurological Examination: Ataxic gait noted. Right Upper Limb Strength: 4/5. Coordination Tests: Evidence of ataxia. Vital Signs: All within normal range (Normothermic, Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, Respiratory Rate).

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your history of natalizumab use and new ataxia, strongly indicate Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
